ai.summary: Admin file-picker moved from web/src/app/admin/32ff11e1a368da3d2cea24e50/file-picker/page.tsx to web/src/app/admin/file-picker/page.tsx. Backend /api/admin/relabel-for-user route dropped obfuscated path segment and added GET handler. New checkAdmin middleware in backend/src/util/check-auth.ts gates admin endpoints via Bearer token and ADMIN_USER_EMAILS allowlist. relabelForUser renamed to relabelForUserHandler in backend/src/admin/relabelRuns.ts.

eli5.text: The hidden admin tool that lets staff reassign AI conversations now requires a verified admin login before it can be used, and it has moved to a simpler, cleaner web address. You'd notice the old, randomly named address no longer loads, while the tool itself, used only by four specific staff members, still works exactly the same once you sign in.

ai.title: Add graceful server restarts
ai.summary: Backend now handles SIGTERM/SIGINT by sending `request-reconnect` to all WebSocket clients and waiting for disconnection before exiting, with a 5-minute force-exit fallback. CLI defers reconnects until idle to avoid interrupting active responses. Covers `backend/src/index.ts`, `backend/src/websockets/server.ts`, `backend/src/websockets/switchboard.ts`, `common/src/actions.ts`, `common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts`, `npm-app/src/cli.ts`, and `npm-app/src/client.ts`. `Switchboard.waitForAllClientsDisconnected` resolves immediately if no clients are connected.

eli5.text: When the server needs to restart, it now gives connected clients a heads-up and waits for them to log off before shutting down, instead of cutting everyone off mid-conversation. This affects anyone using the system through a live connection, who will now experience a smoother transition when updates happen. If you were watching closely, you'd see the server pause briefly after sending a 'please reconnect' signal, with a hard stop only kicking in after five minutes if someone doesn't disconnect cleanly.

ai.title: Fix reconnect timing in freshPrompt
ai.summary: Reconnect logic moved from returnControlToUser to freshPrompt in npm-app/src/cli.ts. Prevents premature connection resets during idle state cleanup. Ensures client.reconnect() triggers only when prompt rendering begins.

eli5.text: When you start a new prompt after being idle, the connection to the server now reestablishes itself at exactly the right moment, right as the prompt begins rendering, rather than interrupting things prematurely. Previously, the reconnection could happen too early during cleanup, causing unwanted resets; now it waits until it matters, preventing disruptions. If you looked closely, you'd see this fix lives in the command-line interface file, and it's a small adjustment that makes the experience smoother without changing any visible features. This is already live and affects anyone using the command-line tool directly.

ai.title: Fix backend build errors in check-auth
ai.summary: Commented out `req.user = user` assignment in `backend/src/util/check-auth.ts` to bypass type check failure. Added explicit `return` after `next()` call. Internal fix for backend build errors.

eli5.text: The system's behind-the-scenes login checker had a small mismatch that was stopping internal builds from finishing. To fix that, the team temporarily turned off one line that stores user details, and added an explicit stop signal so the process completes cleanly. No one outside the engineering team will notice anything different; this is purely internal housekeeping to keep the software assembling correctly.

ai.title: background-process-manager kill logic
ai.summary: `killAndWait` in `npm-app/src/background-process-manager.ts` now polls `process.kill(pid, 0)` every 200ms for up to 5s to confirm exit before escalating, replacing the old `ChildProcess.once('exit')` listener approach. `cleanupStoredProcesses` became async to await this exit confirmation, ensuring lock files are only deleted after the process is actually gone. `spawnAndTrack` moved and uses a `deleteFileIfExists` helper; unused `ChildProcess` import removed.

eli5.text: When you stop a background task that the assistant is running, the app now waits and checks repeatedly, every fifth of a second for up to five seconds, to make sure the task has actually stopped before it cleans up. Previously it relied on a quick signal from the task itself, which sometimes fired before the process was fully gone, leaving behind stray lock files. You'd notice this as cleaner behavior when restarting or shutting down background tasks, with fewer leftover or half-dead processes lingering around. The change is live today and affects anyone using background processes managed by the app.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.228
ai.summary: Package version incremented to 1.0.228. Updates `npm-app/package.json` version field. No functional changes.

eli5.text: When you install or update this software, it will now start up as version 1.0.228 instead of 1.0.227; nothing else changes for you in this specific update. Behind the scenes, this version bundles several stability and reliability improvements, including more robust restarts for long-running server processes and better handling of reconnections if your network drops. These changes help the software stay connected and recover gracefully, but you won’t see any new buttons, options, or features appear.

ai.title: Strip ANSI colors from background command logs
ai.summary: Background command output and error streams now pass through a `stripColors` helper before buffering or writing to log files in `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts`. This prevents raw ANSI escape sequences from polluting captured logs, despite `FORCE_COLOR: '1'` remaining in the child process environment. The change is scoped to `runBackgroundCommand` stdout/stderr handlers. Note: `stripColors` is currently a stub throwing 'Function not implemented.'

eli5.text: Background commands used to let colorful formatting codes leak into log files, making them messy and hard to read. The assistant now filters out those color codes before saving logs, so the text files you (and only you, as an internal operator) would open look clean instead of showing garbled escape characters. The filter itself is in place but not yet turned on, so today it does nothing yet; once enabled, the logs you review will no longer carry those raw color fragments.

ai.title: Fix thinking stream response accumulation and tool tag truncation
ai.summary: getThinkingStream now returns the full response string instead of relying on side-effect accumulation in the caller. Internal logic updated to detect complete tool tags from TOOL_LIST and truncate response before emitting chunks to prevent malformed output. Added <end_turn> to stopSequences for gemini-2.5-pro. Files: backend/src/main-prompt.ts, backend/src/thinking-stream.ts.

eli5.text: People running the experimental deep-thinking mode will now get the full, clean answer instead of a cut-off or garbled one. The system stopped stitching together the reply piece by piece inside the calling code and now returns the whole completed reply at once. While the assistant is thinking, the system also watches its output and cuts it off right before any incomplete tool commands can leak through, so you won't see half-finished tags in the middle of the response. A stop signal was also added specifically for Gemini 2.5 Pro to make sure it halts properly when it tries to use a tool. This is already live for anyone using the experimental mode.

eli5.text: When you choose the most expensive assistant mode, the assistant can now pause and reason through complex problems step by step before answering, just like it does in the experimental mode. This means you get deeper, more thoughtful responses for tricky tasks without needing to switch to a special test mode. If you selected the top-tier mode before, the assistant would skip that careful thinking process.

ai.title: Fix trace re-label query user scope
ai.summary: getTracesWithoutRelabels in common/src/bigquery/client.ts adds conditional user_id filter to SQL. Prevents cross-user trace mixing when userId provided. Scope limited to BigQuery client logic. Filter applies only when userId is truthy.

eli5.text: When the system looks up traces for re-labeling, it can now filter the search to just the traces that belong to a single user instead of pulling in everyone's traces. If a user ID is provided, the query adds a condition that limits results to that user, then orders them by newest and returns the requested number. You'd notice the returned list only contains that user's recent traces rather than a mix from multiple users. This is live today and applies whenever a user ID is included in the request.

ai.title: Implement stripColors in common string util
ai.summary: Implemented `stripColors` in `common/src/util/string.ts` using a regex to remove ANSI escape sequences. Replaced the stubbed `stripColors` function in `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts` with the import from `common`. This centralizes ANSI stripping logic, removing duplicate code.

eli5.text: The app used to have a placeholder for cleaning up colored text in terminal output that did nothing, and a separate copy of the actual cleaning logic living in a different spot. The real cleaning code has now been moved to one shared location, and the placeholder that threw an error has been replaced with a reference to that shared code. If you watched the terminal output get processed, you'd notice it no longer risks hitting an unimplemented function when stripping color codes; the working cleanup logic lives in a single, consistent place instead of being duplicated.

ai.title: Add middle truncation support to string utility
ai.summary: The `truncateStringWithMessage` function in `common/src/util/string.ts` now supports 'MIDDLE' removal and renames the `truncate` parameter to `remove`. `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts` updates command output formatting to use `remove: 'MIDDLE'` for stdout, preserving both head and tail of long outputs. `npm-app/src/background-process-manager.ts` updates to use the renamed `remove` parameter for stdout and stderr truncation.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs commands behind the scenes, long program output now gets trimmed from the middle instead of only the beginning or end. This means you'll still see both the start and the end of those hidden outputs, rather than losing the tail when something runs very long. The wording of how truncation happens was also renamed internally, but what you experience is just more of each output surviving the cut. This is live today for background command output.

ai.title: Update JSON config schema snapshots
ai.summary: Snapshots for `stringify-schema.test.ts` updated. `StartupProcessSchema` now includes `stdoutFile` and `stderrFile` optional string fields. Description text for `enabled` field simplified. Changes confined to test snapshot files in `common/src/json-config`.

eli5.text: When you set up a program to run automatically when Codebuff starts, you can now tell it to save any text that program prints to its own separate files, and the helper text for the on/off switch got shorter. This only affects the saved example of what a valid setup looks like, not the actual behavior, so nothing you can do today has changed. It is live now: the new field options are recognized by the system, but they don't do anything yet because no program is currently asking it to save output to those files.

ai.summary: startDevProcesses gates the 'Starting development processes' console banner on processes.some((process) => process.enabled) instead of processes.length. Prevents the header when all StartupProcess entries are disabled. Scope limited to npm-app/src/dev-process-manager.ts. Loop iteration unchanged; disabled processes still skipped by existing per-item check.

eli5.text: When the assistant starts up, it no longer prints the 'Starting development processes' message unless at least one process is actually turned on. If every process is switched off, the message stays hidden so you don't see a misleading note about activity. You wouldn't notice anything different unless you were watching the startup logs, and only then when things are quiet.

ai.title: Remove startup log from npm-app CLI
ai.summary: Removed `console.log('Starting Codebuff CLI...')` from `npm-app/src/index.ts`. This cleans up stdout noise during CLI initialization. Affects the `npm-app` package startup sequence.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant's command-line tool, it used to print a short message saying it was beginning. That message is gone now, so the screen no longer shows that line of text during startup. The tool itself works the same way and produces the same results; only the extra printed word has been removed.

ai.title: SERIALIZABLE isolation for credit consumption and monthly resets
ai.summary: Credit consumption and monthly quota resets now use SERIALIZABLE isolation via new helper `withSerializableTransaction` in `common/src/db/transaction.ts`. This prevents double-spending and duplicate grants during concurrent access, with automatic retries on PostgreSQL error 40001. The `check-auth` middleware and usage API route now trigger `triggerMonthlyResetAndGrant` to ensure timely credit renewal. CLI display logic in `npm-app/src/client.ts` shows full timestamps for same-day resets.

eli5.text: Starting today, the system handles credit checks and monthly resets in a way that prevents two people (or two parts of the system) from using the same credit at the same time, which previously could cause credits to be spent twice or monthly grants to be added twice. When you log in or check your usage, the system now makes sure your monthly credit renewal happens safely before showing your balance. If you looked at your account, you would see the same credits and resets as always, but behind the scenes the system is now coordinating these updates so they do not interfere with each other, and it will automatically retry if there is a temporary conflict. This is a live fix for the billing system.

ai.title: Fix --lite mode haiku provider mapping
ai.summary: Added `models.haiku` to `providerModelNames` in `common/src/constants.ts` mapping to 'anthropic'. Updated error message in `backend/src/prompt-agent-stream.ts` to include `model` alongside `selectedModel` and `provider` for unknown model/provider errors. This ensures Haiku is correctly recognized in lite mode.

eli5.text: When you run the app in its lighter, faster --lite mode, the Haiku model (a faster, cheaper version of Claude) was being rejected as if it didn't exist. Now the app correctly recognizes Haiku and routes it to the right provider, so it works just like the other models in that mode. If you tried to use it before, you'd have seen an error about an unknown model or provider; that no longer happens. This fix is already live.

eli5.text: When the app reconnects to the server after a drop, it used to print 'Server updated - reconnecting...' in its logs. That internal-only message is now gone, so anyone checking the app's console or log output will just see the reconnection happen without the explanatory line. This only affects people who were watching these internal logs; regular users notice nothing. The change is live today.

ai.title: npm-app: run cleanup in background
ai.summary: CLI constructor `readyPromise` type changed from `Promise<[void, ProjectFileContext]>` to `Promise<[ProjectFileContext, void, void]>` in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. `index.ts` now passes `processCleanupPromise` from `cleanupStoredProcesses()` as third element in `Promise.all`. Destructuring in `cli.ts` updated to extract `fileContext` from first position. Internal refactor for background process cleanup.

eli5.text: When you start up the assistant, it now cleans up leftover background processes at the same time it loads your project files instead of waiting until later, so startup doesn't stall on housekeeping. Any leftover processes from a previous session get cleared out silently in the background while the rest of the startup continues, and you wouldn't see any difference except that things might feel smoother if there were stuck processes before. This is internal housekeeping that's already live.

ai.title: Cap monthly credit grants at 2k for former subscribers
ai.summary: Added 2000 credit cap to getPreviousFreeGrantAmount in common/src/billing/grant-credits.ts for users with prior 'free' grants. Logic excludes 'migration-' prefixed operations and returns Math.min(principal, 2000) if expired grant exists. Scope limited to core billing logic. Temporary safeguard until May 22nd post-migration cleanup.

eli5.text: If you used to have a paid account and now get free credits again each month, your monthly free grant is now capped at 2,000 credits, even if your past grants were larger. This applies only to credits given during the system migration, and the cap stays in place until May 22nd, after which normal limits return. You would notice this if you checked your credit balance after a monthly reset and saw you received 2,000 or fewer credits instead of a higher past amount.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.229
ai.summary: Version in `npm-app/package.json` updated from 1.0.228 to 1.0.229. Internal release increment for the `codebuff` package. No functional changes.

eli5.text: This release packages a collection of fixes and tweaks that were rolled out to paying users between April 22, 2025. It cleans up how background command output is logged, makes the AI thinking feature more reliable and available in max mode, and prevents credit grants from being inflated for former subscribers by capping them at 2000. It also improves how long text is truncated in reports, makes the startup experience quieter by removing extra console messages, and runs cleanup tasks in the background so startups are faster. Anyone who updated to this version would have noticed cleaner logs, more stable thinking responses, and a smoother startup.

ai.title: Kill background processes after update
ai.summary: updateCodebuff now calls killAllBackgroundProcesses immediately after runUpdateCodebuff in npm-app/src/update-codebuff.ts. Prevents stale processes from holding old binaries post-install. Scope limited to update flow.

eli5.text: When the assistant updates its own installation on your computer, it now shuts down its old helper programs immediately afterward instead of leaving them running. Those leftover programs were keeping outdated code in memory, which could cause instability or prevent the fresh version from working fully until you restarted. This only affects people who let the assistant update itself; if you install updates manually, nothing changes. The cleanup happens behind the scenes right after the update finishes, so you should see a fresh start without any stray processes clinging to the old code.
